To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the interface strength is the most important factor in determining the compressive strength of hollow glass microsphere – resin composites.
the compressive yield strength can be predicted by a theoretical model, if the interface strength of the composite is known.

the effect of surface treatments can be quantitively described using extant theories; the interface strength can be controlled by the matrix composition; and the interface strength is not the only parameter that affects the reinforcing effect of the microspherical particles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of the compressive yield strength and the compressive failure mechanism of hollow glass microsphere (HGM) – epoxy composites.
the development of new composite materials based on hollow glass microspheres and epoxy resin
the development of a new class of composite materials based on hollow glass microspheres (HGMs).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for hollow glass spheres in an epoxy matrix the effect of surface modification on the compressive yield strength can be quantitively predicted by the models of Gibson and Ashby and of Kari and Ashby.
the compressive strength of hollow microsphere composites can be increased by increasing the interface strength.
the interface strength is a major determinant of the compressive yield strength.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
for hollow glass sphere composites with a brittle matrix, the reinforcing effect of the spheres is limited by the stress concentration factor and the interface strength.

the reinforcing effect of hollow glass microsphere –epoxy composites can be described by the theoretical model developed by Hashin and Rosen, provided that the microspheres do not contain any defects and are treated to improve the interfacial strength.
the compressive strength is determined by the strength of the interface between the hollow glass microspheres and the matrix.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the compressive strength of hollow glass microspheres is a function of both the matrix and the microsphere surface treatment.
, by varying the surface treatment, one can modify the reinforcing effect of hollow microspheres in a predictable way.
it is possible to control the interface strength and the reinforcing effect by varying the surface treatment.
